corrected_proposal.title: DHS Ends Cyber Safety Review Board Memberships During Salt Typhoon Review
corrected_proposal.description_short: Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman ended CSRB memberships while the board was reviewing the Salt Typhoon telecom intrusion.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman ended current advisory-committee memberships, including the Cyber Safety Review Board, SANS and TechTarget reported. The board was investigating the 2024 Salt Typhoon telecom intrusion. The sources establish the membership action, but do not show whether the review stopped or what security effects followed.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On January 20, 2025, Acting Department of Homeland Security Secretary Benjamine Huffman issued a memo ending current memberships on DHS advisory committees. SANS and TechTarget reported that the Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB) was included. The CSRB reviews significant cybersecurity incidents and makes recommendations; SANS noted that it had previously examined Log4Shell, Lapsus$ attacks, and the Microsoft Exchange Online breach. At the time of the memo, the board was investigating the 2024 Salt Typhoon intrusion into U.S. telecommunications networks. The reported action ended committee memberships while that review was underway. The sources do not establish whether the investigation stopped permanently, whether the board later resumed work, or what security effects followed. They also do not show that President Trump signed the memo or that the action caused CISA Director Jen Easterly’s separate departure at the presidential transition. This record concerns the membership termination and the contemporaneous review, not a halt to all federal cyber defense work or a measured cybersecurity loss.

source_fact_map.fact: Acting DHS Secretary Benjamine Huffman's January 20 memo terminated advisory committee positions, including CSRB membership.
source_fact_map.quote: An internal memo issued January 20, 2025, from Acting Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Benjamine Huffman, terminated all advisory committee positions. Among those dismissed were the Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB)
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: An internal memo issued January 20, 2025, from Acting Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Benjamine Huffman, terminated all advisory committee positions. Among those dismissed were the Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB), a committee responsible for “study[ing] major cyber incidents and recommend[ing] improvements,” comprising private sector experts and government cybersecurity officials. Since its establishment in 2022 by President Biden's executive order, the CSRB investigated the Log4Shell security crisis, attacks by Lapsus$, and the Microsoft Exchange Online Breach, and at the time of Huffman's memo was in the process of investigating the massive 2024 breach of US telecommunications networks by the Chinese state-sponsored hacking group, Salt Typhoon.

source_fact_map.fact: The CSRB was investigating Salt Typhoon at the time.
source_fact_map.quote: The Cyber Safety Review Board was investigating recent attacks by Chinese state-sponsored threat actor Salt Typhoon when DHS terminated all advisory board memberships.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The Cyber Safety Review Board was investigating recent attacks by Chinese state-sponsored threat actor Salt Typhoon when DHS terminated all advisory board memberships. By Alexander Culafi, Senior News Writer, Dark Reading. Published: 27 Jan 2025. Former members of the Department of Homeland Security's Cyber Safety Review Board have been broadly silent on their dismissals last week. Benjamine C. Huffman, who was the acting DHS secretary prior to Kristi Noem's confirmation Saturday, sent a Jan. 20 memo that immediately terminated all current DHS advisory committee memberships. Though not named in the memo directly, this included the Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB), an advisory board established by former President Joe Biden in 2021 to review and report on significant cybersecurity issues and incidents.
